rationale: C03 is an unmistakable drafting template for the child. The two proclamations use the same five-step recital sequence—congressional acceptance of a state constitution, voter approval of required propositions, a general election and certified returns, gubernatorial certification, and a presidential finding that the propositions were adopted and officers elected—followed by an almost verbatim declaration that all procedural requirements were satisfied and admission on an equal footing is accomplished. The substitutions are principally Alaska/Hawaii, dates, statutory citations, and minor office-title wording. C06 has a weaker parallel involving statutory conditions, administrative confirmation, a finding of full compliance, and a consequent proclamation. C18 shares Hawaii-specific statutory and admission language but is a short implementation letter rather than a substantial drafting model.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress of the United States by the act approved on March 18, 1959 ... accepted, ratified, and confirmed the constitution ... and provided for the admission of the State of Hawaii into the Union on an equal footing with the other States upon compliance with certain procedural requirements
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Congress of the United States by the act approved on July 7, 1958 ... accepted, ratified, and confirmed the constitution ... and provided for the admission of the State of Alaska into the Union on an equal footing with the other States of the Union upon compliance with certain procedural requirements
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim opening recital, with the state, dates, statute, and minor phrasing substituted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: a majority of the legal votes cast at an election on June 27, 1959, were in favor of each of the propositions required to be submitted to the people of Hawaii
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a majority of the legal votes cast at an election held on August 26, 1958, were in favor of each of the propositions required to be submitted to the people of Alaska
shared_material.explanation: The second recital uses the same evidentiary finding and sentence structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: a general election was held on July 28, 1959, and ... the returns of the general election were made and certified as provided in the act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a general election was held on November 25, 1958, and ... the returns of the general election were made and certified as provided in the act

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Governor of Hawaii has certified to me the results of the submission ... of the three propositions ... and the results of the general election
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Acting Governor of Alaska has certified to me the results of the submission ... of the three propositions ... and the results of the general election

shared_material.child_excerpt: the procedural requirements imposed by the Congress on the State of Hawaii ... have been complied with in all respects and ... admission ... into the Union on an equal footing with the other States of the Union is now accomplished
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the procedural requirements imposed by the Congress on the State of Alaska ... have been complied with in all respects and ... admission ... into the Union on an equal footing with the other States of the Union is now accomplished
shared_material.explanation: The operative declaration is essentially copied, changing only the state name.
